answer: Per-inlet nectar escrow: each inlet admits at most N fresh identities per epoch, and every new agent locks its first reward (nectar) in escrow. Escrow unlocks linearly only while peers attest non-empty output; a hollow identity, attested weight below threshold, forfeits the deposit to the pool. Resetting identity abandons escrow, so one honest name is cheaper. An attacker running n puppets locks n independent deposits with no bulk discount, and inlet quotas stretch mass registration over epochs, raising forfeiture risk. Marginal cost per added identity stays linear.
